project.proof_overview: Strict promotion is serial and needs fresh candidate and whole-image checks. Isolated research may preserve parser-readable objects that the strict production reader rejects, but cannot promote them.
project.workflow_overview: Compact diagnosis -> machine-level prediction/falsifier -> bounded batch or adaptive experiment -> effective-output grouping -> change analysis level on repeated outcomes -> strict grind/whole-image validation for promotion.

mechanisms.claim: Useful compiler/object evidence and strict recovery are different states; promotion requires immutable oracle inputs and fresh whole-image proof.
mechanisms.scope: Method is reusable; Stunts MZ/OMF and queue contracts are not.

mechanisms.claim: After two source hypotheses yield the same profile/context-aware effective output, move to a different analysis level; changed source text is not progress.

mechanisms.claim: Report anchors, islands, operand mappings, contradicting uses and residuals separately; a pattern is not variable identity or a repair.
mechanisms.scope: Implementation assumes x86-16 decoding but evidence discipline is portable.

mechanisms.claim: Pinned compiler syntax limits and strict parser/binder omissions can be demonstrated blockers, distinct from a source-search or model limitation.

mechanisms.scope: MSC5.0/5.1 Stunts listing/pristine-image mapping. Mapping is not C ownership; unclassified DB/data remains rejected.
mechanisms.experiments: 234 to 497 verified mappings and 112875 newly mapped code-evidence bytes; nine medium tasks, four strict promotions/28 C bytes. All prior verified intervals retain identities.

mechanisms.claim: Historical LINK parity for a bounded mixed far-CALL/DGROUP-offset object enables two independently bound strict contributions.
mechanisms.scope: One public/full UNIT_TEXT; one zero-addend external target-frame pointer32 CALL plus reviewed external DGROUP offset16 obligations; no extra contributions, arbitrary frames or callback pointers.
mechanisms.experiments: Four historical LINK controls: two orders within each MSC5.00/5.10 profile; complete 32-byte parity. Independent data evidence then admits free_sdgame2 18 bytes and locate_text_res 52 bytes through whole-image proof.

trajectories.outcome: Mixed controls succeeded in both arms; unresolved cases remained unresolved; retain Luna/high first as an engineering decision, not capability proof.

trajectories.outcome: Batch reduced worker requests/time/cost in one pair but produced fewer unique outputs and no strict recovery; use small independent batches only.
sequence: retain sequential feedback for dependent pivots

trajectories.outcome: Declaration order explained BP-home mapping but left 194/200 extent gap; independent return-label fixture refuted a simple epilogue-placement hypothesis.

negatives.claim: No Astra-only strict solve in four matched pairs; no Astra-first class or population solve curve follows.
Direct worker cost omits material supervision/auto-review overhead; do not report it as end-to-end recovery economics.
One batch pair saved worker resources but found fewer outputs and no strict match; optimal batch size is unknown.
Early return and explicit trailing zero-return label emitted identical 38-byte MSC 5.1 fixtures.
negatives.scope: two complete fixtures, not all control-flow spellings

negatives.claim: With declaration order fixed, the tested negative-polarity condition emitted a third 194-byte output, lost two late anchors and did not reach the AL/CBW target sequence.
negatives.scope: one source form under pinned MSC 5.1, not all return expressions or TU contexts

negatives.claim: Tested _based/_segname forms were rejected by pinned MSC 5.10 and did not select the needed CODE-segment access.
Broader binding cannot repair the observed wrong source extents in the selected current candidate archive.
negatives.scope: 64 distinct task/object payloads across 28 remaining supervisor tasks; not a population estimate.
negatives.result: 60 have different extents; only set_frame_callback is equal-extent and fully nonfixup-exact among four equal-size candidates. Callback/data ownership remains unproved.
